questions.question: The process of breaking down of rocks by the action of wind, water and climate is called as ______.
questions.solution:
**Option 4** is the correct answer.

**Weathering:**

 
• The breaking down of rocks into smaller fractions is called weathering. The disintegration of rocks can take place due to a number of factors like temperature changes, exposure to chemicals in the atmosphere, vegetation growth, etc. Broadly weathering is classified into three types:
 
 
• Physical.
 
• Chemistry.
 
• Biological.
 
 

 
 

 **Type of weathering**
 **How it takes place**
 
 

 Physical
 
 
 
• Repeated temperature changes.
 
• Shattering caused by precipitation.
 
• Exfoliation caused by wind.
 
• Frost and thaw action.
 
 
 
 

 Chemical
 
 
 
• Solution. (when exposed to water).
 
• Oxidation/Carbonation (reaction with gases present in the atmosphere).
 
 
 
 

 Biological
 
 
 
• Brought about by animals.
 
• Brought about by plants.
 
 
 
 

 

 
 

 **Process**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Landslide 
 
 
 
• A rapid and sudden movement of a large mass of rock or soil down a slope.
 
• It can be caused by an earthquake, volcano, Heavy Rainfall, Slope failure, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Erosion
 
 
 
• Removal of the loosely bound top layer of soil.
 
• It can be brought about by the wind, flowing water, Movement of animals, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Solifluction
 
 
 
• The gradual downslope movement of completely saturated soil or rock fragments.

questions.question: Who presided over the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3.**

 
• Drafting Committee was constituted by the Constituent Assembly **on August 29. 1947.**
 
• This committee was assigned the** task of preparing a draft of the constitution.**
 
• It was a seven-member committee **headed by Dr. BR Ambedkar.**
 
• NG Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Dr. KM Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah and, NM Rau and TT Krishnamacharya were the other 6 members.
 
• Drafting Committee presented the** first draft of the Constitution** in** February 1948 and** it had** 315 Articles **and** 9 Schedules.**

questions.question: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added which part to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2**. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added Part IX to the Indian Constitution.

 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act Was enacted passed in 1992 during the Narasimha Rao Government.
 
• It added Part IX to our Constitution which is entitled as 'The Panchayats' and deals with the provisions of Articles 243 to 243 O.
 
• A new schedule, the Eleventh Schedule was also added to the Constitution.
 
• This act leads to the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati raj system for local self-government.
 
• The three-tier system consists of:
 
 
• Zila Parishad (at the district level).
 
• Block Samiti (at block level).
 
• Gram Panchayat (at village level).

questions.question: The Archaeological Site of Inamgaon is situated in ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Inamgaon is an archaeological site located in the **Pune district of Maharashtra.**
 
• The site is located on the **Bank of river Ghod.**
 
• The excavations have revealed their association with** Malwa Culture, Early Jorwe Culture, and Late Jorwe Culture** which correspond to 1600 to 1400 BC, 1400 to 1000 BC, and 1000 to 700 BC respectively.
 
• The majority of earthenware found there corresponds to **Malwa Culture i.e. Black Painted Red Ware.**
 
• The house structure corresponds to all three cultures.
 
• The** site is also famous for the strange burial of 35 years old man**.
 
• The **skeletal remains of a man** which date back to 1000 BC were placed in a four-legged jar and were buried in the courtyard of a house.

questions.question: Which comoponent of blood ﬁghts against germs that enter human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**White blood cells.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **WBCs **fight against the germs that enter the human body.
 
• Also known as **leukocytes**** **are a part of the immune system of our body.
 
• These are produced in Bone Marrow and have an average lifetime of 3-4 days.
 
• WBCs produces antibodies and ingest foreign material to fight infection.
 
• These are of three types lymphocytes, granulocytes, and monocytes.
 
 
• **Lymphocytes**: These are further classified as T and B cells.
 
 
• **T cells **recognize the infected cells.
 
• **B cells **secrete antibodies.
 
 
 
• **Granulocytes**: These help the body to get rid of large pathogens like protozoa. Granulocytes are further divided into neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils.
 
• **Monocytes**: These are also known as Scavenger cells. Destroys the pathogens at the site of infection and clears debris.
 
 

 
 

 **Component of Blood**
 **Characteristics**
 
 

 RBC
 
 
 
• Also known as Erythrocytes.
 
• Produced in: Spleen, Liver and Bone Marrow.
 
• Average lifetime: 120 days.
 
• It contains hemoglobin that carries oxygen to all parts of the body.
 
• Carry carbon dioxide to the lungs.
 
 
 
 

 Platelets
 
 
 
• Also known as Thrombocytes.
 
• Produced in: Bone marrow.
 
• Average lifetime: 3-7 days.
 
• ​Help in blood clotting.
 
 
 
 

 Hemoglobin
 
 
 
• It is a metalloprotein present in RBCs.
 
• Helps in the transport of oxygen and Carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Union Budget and Railway Budget of India were merged in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3**. **The announcement regarding the merger was made in 2016 and the first merged bill was introduced on 1st February 2017.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The practice of a **separate budget for Railways was started in 1924**.
 
• It was done on the **recommendations of the Acworth Committee.**
 
• At that time the** railway budget constituted around 84% of the total budget** and therefore it was recommended to separate it from the general budget.
 
• But with a time budget of other ministries also started increasing and some of them even overtook the budget of Railways.
 
• **In 2016 the railway budget shrank to almost 15% of the total budget** and hence the idea to merge it with the general budget was proposed by the Union government in 2016.
 
• **On February 1, 2017, the first combined budget **was presented in parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Budget:**

 
• In our Constitution, the term** 'budget' finds no mention**.
 
• The term** 'Annual Financial Statement'** refers to budget and **article 112 deals** with provisions related to it.
 
• Budget is** prepared by the Department of Economic Affairs**, Ministry of Finance
 
• Finance Minister presents the budget in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The budget is** presented on February 1. **But before 2017, it used to be presented on the last day of February.

questions.question: Sunil Arora has been appointed as the 23rd ______ of India.
questions.solution:
**Option 1** is the correct answer. 

__
 
• Sunil Arora was appointed as the **23rd Chief Election Commissioner of India.**
 
• He assumed the office on December 2, 2018, and **Succeeded Om Prakash Rawat.**

**Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners:**

 
• Chief Election Commissioner is **appointed by the President.**
 
• There are** two election Commissioners also** who have equal powers as that of CEC.
 
• CEC along with the other two Election Commissioners receives the **same salaries & allowances as available to a judge of the Supreme Court.**
 
• They remain in the office for a** term of 6 years or before the completion of 65 years of their age,** whichever is earlier.

**Election Commission:**

 
• **Article 324** of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the Election commission.
 
• It is a permanent and independent body.
 
• It is entrusted with the task to conduct fair **elections to the office of President, Vice-President, Parliament, and State Legislature.**

questions.question: Which article of Indian Constitution guarantees Protection of Life and Personal Liberty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3.**

 
• **Article 21 **of the Indian Constitution provides for Protection of Life and Personal Liberty.
 
• According to this article that no person shall be deprived of its life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by the law.
 
• It is available to both citizens and non-citizens.
 
• Under this article, a number of rights have been declared by the Supreme Court for e.g. Right to live with human dignity, livelihood, privacy, shelter, free legal aid, hearing Information and many more.

questions.question: Deﬁciency of which hormone in the body causes 'Goitre'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2.** Deficiency of **Thyroxine hormone** causes Goitre.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Goiter is a disease in which **swelling occurs in the Thyroid gland **present in your neck.
 
• Thyroxine is a hormone that is secreted into the bloodstream by the thyroid gland.
 
• This hormone** ****plays a vital role in the proper functioning of Heart, Digestive system, metabolic activities etc.**
 
• Iodine is the main component of Thyroxine hormone and deficiency of former leads to deficient production of the latter by the thyroid gland.
 
• Thyroid then works extra hard to produce the requisite Thyroxine hormone which leads to swelling in it and hence Goitre. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/013b4cb278b3fbf4d2ca1b5ea2f465fb9599ad32733c08462d1d9912c9a1edab.png] 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Hormone**
 **Facts**
 
 

 Adrenaline
 
 
 
• Also known as Epinephrine.
 
• Produced by Adrenal glands and neurons in Medulla Oblongata.
 
• Increases Heartbeat, opens Bronchioles.
 
• Secreted in response to fear, panic or threat.
 
 
 
 

 Thyroxine
 
 
 
• Also known as T4; Tetraiodothyronine.
 
• Released by the Thyroid gland.
 
• Plays a vital role in the proper functioning of Heart, Digestive system, metabolic activities, etc.
 
 
 
 

 Estrogen
 
 
 
• Sex hormones of women.
 
• Produced by Ovaries and Adrenal Glands.
 
• It causes the growth of women's physical features during puberty.
 
 
 
 

 Testosterone
 
 
 
• Mainly produced in men by Testicles.
 
• Plays a vital role in the development of male reproductive organs and sperm production.

• **Tributaries**: Rapti, Budhi Ganga, and Chhoti Gandhaki are the major tributaries.

**Son:**

 
• River son originates from **Amarkantak, Madhya Pradesh** and then flows for 1043 km before joining river Ganga.
 
• Flows through states of Madhya Pradesh, Jharkhand and **joins river Ganga near Patna**.
 
• Anuppur, Deori, and Sonbhadra are the major towns situated on its Banks.
 
• **Tributaries:** Rihand, Chhoti Mahanadi and North Koel are the major tributaries.

questions.question: What is the chemical name of table salt?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 1.**

 
• **Sodium Chloride** is commonly known as table salt.
 
• Its chemical formula is **NaCl** and both Sodium & Chloride are** present in 1:1**.
 
• It is a crystalline sloid generally **obtained from Seawater.**
 
• **The pH** of table salt in water is almost** 7** and hence neutral.
 
• **Uses:**
 
 
• **It is used in the food industry as a** flavoring agent and for preservation.
 
• In the chemical manufacturing industry.
 
• It is sprinkled on roads covered with ice to **speed up the melting of ice**.
 
 
 
• It also has biological significance and **helps the human body to absorb and transport nutrients, maintain Blood Pressure and fluid balance, etc.**
